=== PMID: 10755569 ===

Title: ICAM-1 deficiency suppresses host allosensitization and rejection of MHC-disparate corneal transplants.

Journal/Date: Transplantation (2000)

MeSH Keywords: Animals, Blood Group Incompatibility, Corneal Transplantation, Graft Rejection, Graft Survival, Hypersensitivity, Delayed, Immunization, Intercellular Adhesion Molecule-1


--- ABSTRACT ---
[BACKGROUND]: We used a murine model of orthotopic corneal transplantation to determine whether host deficiency in ICAM-1 promotes survival of corneal grafts with different degrees of allodisparity.
[METHODS]: ICAM-1-/- and wild-type C57BL/6 (ICAM-1+/+) received corneal grafts from the following strains of mice: BALB/c (fully mismatched), BALB.b (mismatched at multiple minor H only), or B10.D2 [including major histocompatibility complex (MHC) mismatch]. Graft rejection, induction of allospecific delayed-type hypersensitivity (DTH) responses, and leukocytic infiltration of grafts were measured.
[RESULTS]: There were no differences in long-term survival of allografts that were either fully mismatched or had only minor H disparity in ICAM-1+/+ vs. ICAM-1-/-hosts. However, whereas B10.D2 grafts were accepted in only 58% of the ICAM-1+/+ hosts, graft survival in ICAM-1-/- recipients was 100% (P=0.006). Moreover, none of the ICAM-1-/- mice receiving B10.D2 grafts developed allospecific DTH.
[CONCLUSIONS]: Prolonged survival seen in MHC-mismatched grafts in ICAM-1-/- mice, along with a suppressed DTH response to donor alloantigens after transplantation, suggest that ICAM-1 is associated with recipient sensitization to MHC alloantigens.

key_findings.finding: The primary experimental study is Sonoda et al., “ICAM-1 deficiency suppresses host allosensitization and rejection of MHC-disparate corneal transplants” (Transplantation, 2000; PMID 10755569). It used orthotopic murine corneal transplantation in ICAM-1−/− versus wild-type C57BL/6 (ICAM-1+/+) recipients, with BALB/c, BALB.b, or B10.D2 donor corneas; the study directly assessed graft rejection/survival, donor-allospecific delayed-type hypersensitivity (DTH), and leukocyte infiltration.

source_tools.relevance: Primary paper abstract and bibliographic details

key_findings.finding: ICAM-1 deficiency protected specifically against the MHC-disparate B10.D2 grafts: long-term graft acceptance was 100% in ICAM-1−/− recipients versus 58% in wild-type recipients (P=0.006), and none of the ICAM-1−/− recipients developed donor-alloantigen-specific DTH. This supports suppression of host allosensitization and rejection in the MHC-mismatched setting.

The effect was not general across all disparities: there was no difference between ICAM-1−/− and wild-type hosts in long-term survival of fully mismatched BALB/c grafts or BALB.b grafts mismatched only at multiple minor histocompatibility antigens. Thus, the conclusion is qualified as mismatch-dependent and strongest for the tested B10.D2 MHC disparity, rather than evidence that ICAM-1 deficiency universally prevents corneal rejection.

source_tools.relevance: Comparison across fully mismatched, minor-H-only, and MHC-mismatched donor strains

key_findings.finding: Available evidence is limited to the single primary mouse study’s abstract; the retrieved record does not provide full-text detail on leukocyte-infiltration results, exact MHC haplotypes/degree of disparity beyond the strain designations, or independent replication. No conflicting experimental result was identified in the retrieved evidence, but the null effects in the BALB/c and BALB.b arms are an important qualification.
